references.title: SeisBench—A Toolbox for Machine Learning in Seismology
references.supports: Interoperable waveform datasets, models, training and evaluation infrastructure. Does not certify each dataset for every scientific task.

references.title: Curated Regional Earthquake Waveforms (CREW) Dataset
references.supports: Section 3 discusses label/data quality and iterative curation; manually screened 10,000 initially assembled examples and flagged 28%. This is not an audit of all SeisBench releases. Final current landing abstract says 1.6 million waveforms; older indexed copies say 2.3 million, so avoid an unnecessary release-size claim.

references.title: A Global-scale Database of Seismic Phases from Cloud-based Picking at Petabyte Scale
references.status: peer-reviewed data report; published reviewer reports
references.supports: Demonstrated inference over 1.3 PB, producing 4.3 billion picks from 47,354 stations, with around 145,000 jobs under three days. It is inference/data mining, not foundation-model training or proof of independent replication.

references.title: Complex multi-fault rupture and triggering during the 2023 earthquake doublet in southeastern Türkiye
references.supports: Strong-motion and teleseismic waveforms and static/high-rate GNSS jointly constrain rupture; satellite observations constrain fault geometry and provide comparisons. Multimodal scientific integration, not joint multimodal neural-network training. Does not estimate prevalence or temporal growth.

references.title: Deep learning in multimodal remote sensing data fusion: A comprehensive review
references.venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
references.supports: Section 2 searches WoS topic remote sensing AND deep learning AND fusion: 691 original results, 598 articles 2015–2022. Broader remote sensing AND fusion comparator: 4,403 articles. Figure 2 reports increasing annual counts and DL share. Scope is keyword-selected remote-sensing fusion, not all geosciences or a hand-verified modality count. Section 3 includes LiDAR-optical, SAR-optical, and remote sensing/geospatial big data; contradicts categorical claims that heterogeneous fusion has never been done.

references.title: OlmoEarth: Stable Latent Image Modeling for Multimodal Earth Observation
references.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
references.status: peer-reviewed conference proceeding; official CVF BibTeX verified
references.supports: Three satellite modalities (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, Landsat) and six derived maps are genuinely multimodal. Variable native band resolutions and aligned image time series/maps. Thus contrast representation geometry and scientific semantics with point/line waveforms, unstructured simulations, and networks; do not deny cross-modal training.

references.title: A benchmark of seismic picking and detection algorithms
references.status: primary software documentation, not peer-reviewed evidence
references.supports: Official README explicitly says companion benchmark repository is not actively maintained (while core SeisBench remains active); results-summary code and notebooks not generally maintained. Do not claim this proves no leaderboard anywhere exists.

unsupported_claims: No maintained seismic leaderboard anywhere exists
Community has never independently reproduced PB access
Most current geoscientific papers use one modality
Multimodal geoscientific foundation-model training has never been done
Peer-reviewed broad geoscientific modality-count increase already established by this pilot
